records.trigger: red_evidence_required: a registration guard bound to a hardcoded list cannot notice a population member nobody registered, and the guard itself never runs under lattice validate
records.observedFailure: The guard exits 0 while an unregistered member of its own population is present on disk and deliberately exits 1. Its success line reports 'all 3 required red-evidence smokes' - the count comes from REQUIRED_VALIDATE_COMMANDS.length, so it reports the size of the expectation and can never reveal the gap. Verified on this worktree at CLI 0.3.247: the repro command exits 1 having observed the guard exit 0. A separate control confirms the same guard DOES exit non-zero when a listed command is de-registered, so this is blindness rather than a broken guard. Separately measured: 18 of 31 packages/main/tests/red/*.mjs are unregistered, 3 are spawned transitively by red-b2aa7-chk007-receipt.mjs, leaving 15 executed by no automated path - including this guard itself.
records.failingCommand: node -e "const{execFileSync}=require('child_process');const fs=require('fs'),p=require('path');const probe='packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-b49d4probe-smoke.ts';const dist='packages/main/dist/tasks/red-evidence-b49d4probe-smoke.js';fs.writeFileSync(probe,'export {};\n');fs.writeFileSync(dist,'process.exit(1);\n');let out='',code=0;try{out=execFileSync('node',['packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-validate-registration.mjs'],{encoding:'utf8'})}catch(e){code=e.status||1;out=String(e.stdout||'')+String(e.stderr||'')}fs.unlinkSync(probe);fs.unlinkSync(dist);const reg=fs.readFileSync('lattice.config.json','utf8').includes('red-evidence-b49d4probe-smoke');if(code===0&&!reg){console.log('BLIND: guard exited 0 with an unregistered failing population member present');console.log(out.trim().slice(0,200));process.exit(1)}console.log('guard bit; not blind');"
records.note: Repro-first. The command plants a genuine member of the guard's own dist-task population, registered nowhere and exiting 1, runs the real guard, and exits 1 only if the guard reported success anyway; it removes both probe files before asserting, so the tree is left clean. This is the CRASH-equivalent row for a guard defect: the failure is a confident success line, not an error.
